journey.name: ED-10 A save already in flight survives leaving the editor
journey.description:
REGRESSION GUARD. This journey used to assert the defect: `onSave` ran in `viewModelScope`, so popping the editor destroyed the back stack entry, cleared the ViewModel, cancelled the scope and with it the `createTask` call still inside `FakeTaskApi`'s delay. The task was never created, the user was never told, and there was no snackbar behind this one the way there is behind a delete. Filed as issue #18 and now fixed: the write runs on an application-scoped coroutine and only the reporting of it is lifecycle-bound.
Neither half is visible below the device: a unit test cannot pop a back stack entry, and the ViewModel test that covers this cancels `viewModelScope` by hand, which is a stand-in rather than the thing itself.
The latency knob makes the window wide enough to tap Back inside it. The wait afterwards is what separates "landed late" from "never sent".
Preconditions: adb shell am force-stop com.rounds.test.to_dolist adb shell am start -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.MainActivity --es qa_failure_rate 0.0 --es qa_latency_ms 5000

actions.action: Tap the element with the content description "Add task"
Type "Walked out on" into the "Title" field
Immediately tap the element with the content description "Back", before the save completes
Verify that the app returns to the "Tasks" screen
Verify that "Walked out on" is not yet on screen, because the call is still in flight
Wait ten seconds, which is twice the pinned call latency
Verify that "Walked out on" is on screen
Verify that "Walked out on" is the last row in the list
Verify that no error message is on screen
Verify that exactly five elements with the content description "Delete task" are on screen
